subject: Urgent: ZenithPay QPS surge causing 5xxs and latency — need exec intervention
messages:
From: Laura Kim <laura.kim@zenithpay.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: ops@zenithpay.com
Date: Sat, 06 Jun 2026 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden latency and 5xx spike on dedicated pool (ZenithPay account)

Ben —

We started seeing a sharp increase in token latency and intermittent 5xx errors starting ~08:40 PDT. Our logs show QPS rising by ~4x vs baseline and many calls to the reserved endpoint returning 5xx/503s. This is impacting checkouts. I attached a short log sample and a CSV of request rates.

Can you confirm this is on your side and provide ETA for remediation? We are preparing an ops bridge and may need to divert traffic. This is P0 for us.

- Laura
Head of Engineering, ZenithPay

Attachments: zenith-error-samples.log, redwood_qps-metrics-0606.csv
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Laura Kim <laura.kim@zenithpay.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 06 Jun 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency and 5xx spike on dedicated pool (ZenithPay account)

Laura — thanks for the fast heads-up and the logs. I see the spike in your CSV. I'm escalating to Marcus (eng) and Neha (CS).

Immediate answers:
- We're seeing elevated queue depth on the dedicated GPU pool serving your reserved instances; early indicators point to an overflow of long-running prompts plus a sudden surge from a newly enabled batch job in your environment.
- I'm requesting a bridge now; Marcus, can you take a look at host-level metrics and whether we hit the reserved-throughput ceiling?

Next steps for customer: please stand by for the bridge link — we may ask you to temporarily divert a subset of traffic to your hosted fallback if we can't relieve headroom in ~30m.

—Ben
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: Laura Kim <laura.kim@zenithpay.com>
Date: Sat, 06 Jun 2026 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency and 5xx spike on dedicated pool (ZenithPay account)

On Sat, Jun 6, 2026 at 9:28 AM ben_carter@redwood.com wrote:
> Marcus, can you take a look at host-level metrics and whether we hit the reserved-throughput ceiling?

Checked the pool — we saturated the KV cache lane on several GPUs and the scheduler started returning 503s when per-customer token concurrency hit ~2.8x of the expected steady-state (reserved throughput configured for ZenithPay). We also observed a backlog of requests with long context windows; those amplify memory pressure.

Temporary mitigations I spun up (10:40 PDT):
- Dropped non-essential large-context queued requests from a lower-priority tenant spilling into the same rack (reclaimed ~15% headroom).
- Enabled aggressive prefix cache eviction for ZenithPay's model bundle to free KV allocations (risk: cold starts for some sessions).

If that doesn't hold within 20–30m, we should:
1) Failover a percentage (~25%) of ZenithPay flows to their hosted-compatible variant (explicitly allowed per their config).
2) If requested by Sales/CS, apply a temporary uplift to their reserved throughput (manual capacity commit) while we repro root cause.

Marcus
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: Laura Kim <laura.kim@zenithpay.com>, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 06 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency and 5xx spike on dedicated pool (ZenithPay account)

Joining the bridge — I've started a parallel thread with ZenithPay's account team to confirm whether they flipped any batch jobs or changed prompt templates. Laura, any chance a new scheduled job kicked off this morning? Even short-lived fan-out jobs will push concurrency high.

Ben: going to draft a one-pager for Marcus and execs that summarizes the impact and asks (possible credit/uv uplift + CTO call). Priyom, can you prepare contract language around temporary throughput uplift and short-term crediting? We should be ready if customer calls for exec-level remediation.

Neha
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: leadership@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 06 Jun 2026 10:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation summary for execs — ZenithPay P0 (needs leadership decision)

Team — short exec-ready summary to circulate: 
- Impact: ZenithPay (reserved) experiencing sustained QPS jump leading to 5xxs and token latency >600ms for 30+ mins; checkout flows degraded for ~20% of requests.
- Root cause (prelim): sudden surge from customer-side batch jobs + oversized request contexts -> KV cache pressure + scheduler concurrency cap hit.
- Actions taken: SRE reclaimed headroom (15%) and enabled cache eviction; CS engaged customer for mitigation steps.
- Options for execs: 1) Approve a temporary reserved-throughput uplift (manual commit charge) to avoid failover; 2) Approve a one-time credit and require customer to divert to hosted fallback while we investigate; 3) Decline uplift/credit and allow planned failover to hosted variant.

Please reply with preferred option and any constraints. If no reply in 45m, we will proceed with controlled failover of 25% of traffic to prevent data loss and reduce 5xxs.

—Ben
From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: Laura Kim <laura.kim@zenithpay.com>, cfo@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 07 Jun 2026 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation summary for execs — ZenithPay P0 (needs leadership decision)

Looping leadership and finance after review. Quick note: uplift for the week is feasible but needs a PO/commit from customer or an interim credit authorization. If Sales recommends we proceed without PO, we need an approval from Finance (cc'd).

For operations: Marcus, continue current mitigations and prepare runbook steps for a rollback if failover begins. Neha, get written confirmation from ZenithPay that they will temporarily divert the specified endpoints if we trigger hosted failover.

I'll be on standby for the next 2 hours to authorize emergency uplift if Sales secures customer buy-in.

Priyom
VP, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
